about.text: Fermented camel milk from the pastoralist herds of northern Kenya, also spelled suusa. Raw camel milk is left to sour by itself, with no starter culture. Its containers are first fumigated with smoke from particular woods, which helps it keep and gives it a smoky taste. Women do the processing.

links.name: African Journal of Food, Agriculture, Nutrition and Development (2013)

how.label: ferment in smoked gourd
how.text: Kenyan and Somali suusac is raw camel milk left to sour in gourds smoked with acacia twigs. The smoke flavours and colours it, while wild lactic acid bacteria and yeasts make the acid.

links.name: Jans et al., Int. J. Food Microbiol. (2013)
